diagram_classification: cosmological (elemental and qualitative scheme, with a likely link to the four seasons or the four winds)
interpretation: The diagram most likely shows the four elements and their qualities. A green outer square holds an inner orange rhombus. Four pale circles sit at its corners, at the top, bottom, left and right. Four coloured circles stand in the corners of the square: dark red with a grid, pale grey-blue, dark grey-black and green. These coloured circles probably stand for the four elements: fire (red), air (pale), earth (dark) and water (green). The rhombus connects the four cardinal nodes, which probably mark the cardinal points, the solstices and equinoxes, or the four qualities (hot, cold, wet, dry). The rhombus would then express the pairing of opposites and the links between adjacent elements. The thin vertical and horizontal lines inside the rhombus form a cross or axis. They may mark the central point or the four directions, or the division into quarters. The scheme probably illustrates the harmony of the cosmos or microcosm, in the tradition of the Isidorian and Bedan 'De natura rerum' diagrams. The identification of specific elements is uncertain because there are no labels.
evidence: Visible: a square frame with four corner marks, an inner rhombus of orange bands with a circle at each vertex, four coloured circles in the corners (dark red gridded, pale grey, black-grey, green), and thin cross lines inside the rhombus. No text is legible, so the interpretation rests on the colour and quaternary structure. External: medieval computistical and natural-philosophical manuscripts often use quaternary schemes of elements, qualities, seasons and winds, and the colours red/fire, pale/air, dark/earth and green/water fit that convention. The classification and the exact assignments are provisional, and the diagram could instead be a seasonal or wind scheme.
